label: HTML
description: Semantic markup, accessibility, forms, media and browser behaviour questions for web app development.

questions.title: What is the purpose of `<!DOCTYPE html>`?
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `<!DOCTYPE html>`?

options.text: It imports the HTML5 specification into the page
It switches the browser into standards mode so CSS and layout follow the spec instead of legacy quirks
It declares the character encoding as UTF-8
It is required for JavaScript to run

questions.explanation: A missing or outdated doctype puts the browser into quirks mode, where box sizing and layout differ. Character encoding is declared separately with `<meta charset="utf-8">`.

questions.title: Why prefer `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` over a page of `<div>` elements?
questions.prompt: Why prefer `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` over a page of `<div>` elements?

options.text: Semantic elements render faster because the browser skips their layout
They convey document structure to browsers, assistive technology and search engines, and give screen-reader users landmarks to navigate by
Only semantic elements can contain text nodes
A `<div>` cannot be styled with CSS

questions.explanation: Landmark roles come for free from semantic elements, which improves keyboard navigation and SEO. Rendering speed is not the reason, and `<div>` is styleable like any other element.

questions.title: Which is the most accessible way to label a text input?
questions.prompt: Which is the most accessible way to label a text input?

options.text: `<input type="text" placeholder="Email">`
`<label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" type="email">`
`<input type="email" title="Email">`
`Email`

questions.explanation: A programmatically associated `<label>` gives the input an accessible name, enlarges the click target and is announced by screen readers. Placeholder text disappears on input and is not a label substitute.

questions.title: What does adding `required` to an `<input>` do?
questions.prompt: What does adding `required` to an `<input>` do?

options.text: Nothing by itself — validation must be written in JavaScript
It enables constraint validation, so submitting an empty value blocks the submit and shows a validation message
It marks the field with a red border in every browser
It only affects how the field is rendered on mobile

questions.explanation: `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `min`/`max` participate in native constraint validation checked on submit, extensible through the Constraint Validation API.

questions.title: What is the difference between `<script defer>` and `<script async>`?
questions.prompt: What is the difference between `<script defer>` and `<script async>`?

options.text: Both download in parallel, but `defer` executes after parsing in document order while `async` executes as soon as it is downloaded
`defer` blocks parsing; `async` does not
`async` keeps document order; `defer` does not
They are equivalent for external scripts

questions.explanation: Both attributes avoid render-blocking downloads. `defer` keeps execution order and runs before `DOMContentLoaded`, so it suits app bundles; `async` suits independent scripts such as analytics.

questions.title: A profile page is at `/users/7` and links to `href="edit"`. Where does it go?
questions.prompt: A profile page is at `/users/7` and links to `href="edit"`. Where does it go?

options.text: `/edit`
`/users/edit`
`/users/7/edit`
It depends on the `<base>` element; otherwise the request fails

questions.explanation: A relative URL resolves against the current document URL, so `edit` resolves to `/users/7/edit`. `/users/edit` would need `href="/users/edit"` or `href="../edit"`.

questions.title: Why does `alt` text matter on ``, and what belongs in it?
questions.prompt: Why does `alt` text matter on ``, and what belongs in it?

options.text: It is only used by search engines to rank the page
It is read by screen readers and shown if the image fails; it should describe the image's purpose, and decorative images should use `alt=""`
It is a tooltip shown on hover, so it should hold a caption
It is required only for PNG images

questions.explanation: `alt` is the accessible replacement for the image. Empty `alt` is the correct way to mark purely decorative images so screen readers skip them instead of reading a file name.

questions.title: Which attributes connect a data cell to its header in a complex table?
questions.prompt: Which attributes connect a data cell to its header in a complex table?

options.text: `scope` on `<td>` and `headers` on `<th>`
`headers` on `<td>` pointing at `id` attributes on the `<th>` cells it belongs to
`aria-label` on every `<td>`
`colspan` and `rowspan`

questions.explanation: For multi-level headers, `<th id="...">` plus `<td headers="...">` associates cells with the right headers. `scope` on `<th>` handles simple tables, and `colspan`/`rowspan` only control layout.

questions.title: A single-page app serves the same `index.html` for every route. What is the consequence?
questions.prompt: A single-page app serves the same `index.html` for every route. What is the consequence?

options.text: None — crawlers execute JavaScript exactly like users
Every route shares one title and description unless the document head is updated per route (or content is pre-rendered/server-rendered), which hurts SEO and link previews
Only the favicon stops loading
The browser caches the wrong route

questions.explanation: Crawler support for client rendering is inconsistent. Per-route metadata (Next.js `metadata`/`generateMetadata`, or prerendering) gives each URL its own title, description and social preview.

questions.title: Which input type is the right choice for a quantity between 1 and 10 that must be keyboard-friendly?
questions.prompt: Which input type is the right choice for a quantity between 1 and 10 that must be keyboard-friendly?

options.text: `<input type="range" min="1" max="10">`
`<input type="number" min="1" max="10" inputmode="numeric">`
`<input type="text" pattern="[1-9]|10">`
`<select>` with ten `<option>` elements

questions.explanation: `type="number"` keeps typing and arrow-key stepping, participates in `min`/`max` validation and still shows a numeric keypad via `inputmode`. A range slider is poor for precise entry and a select adds unnecessary interaction.
